To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of supportive communication, such as acknowledging or encouraging further emotional disclosure when responding to older adults’ emotional distress in homecare is promoted when staff elicit the expression of distress and when the expression refers to an emotion.
the use of emotion-focused responses in home care was promoted by nursing staff eliciting the emotional expression, as well as patients’ expression referring to an emotion.
nursing staff in home care responded most often by moderately person-centred communication and acknowledging the older people’s emotional expressions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of supportive, person-centre communication in home care, a topic of great importance for the health of older people.
the quality of the communication between nursing staff and older patients in home care.
the question of whether and how nursing staff’s supportive communication can contribute to healthy aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nursing staff in home care responded to emotional expressions in a person-centred supportive manner, and that this was most often the case when the patient expressed the emotions themselves, rather than when nursing staff eliciting the expressions.

nursing staff responded with supportive communication when older people expressed their emotional distress, and that this response was most frequent when nursing staff elicitation and the patient’s expression referred to an explicit emotion.
nursing staff responded to older patients’ expressions of emotional distress in a supportive manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nursing staff’s responses were supportive in the majority of cases and the use of emotion-focused responses were promoted by elicitation of the expression and by patients’ expressions that refer to emotions.
the use of person-centred supportive care in the form of emotion-focused responses to older people's emotional expressions in home care is a promising strategy for promoting healthy ageing.
nursing staff responded most often with moderately person-centred responses when older people expressed their emotional distress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important for nursing staff to be aware of their own and the older person’s emotional expressions and to use person-centred communication to acknowledge distress and encourage further disclosure of emotion.
the use of supportive communication is a promising strategy in the care of older people.
nursing staff should be encouraged to elicit emotional distress, and to respond to it with person-centred communication.
